text:
sam_support: @lina thanks for filing — we investigated the Go SDK streaming error you sent. Root cause looks like the client-side scanner hitting a buffer/ framing issue when the server sends large chunked JSON fragments.

lina_customer: repro steps I gave: long streaming response with multiple JSON objects (no newline between objects), Go app using bufio.Scanner to read by token then json.Unmarshal => intermittent 'unexpected end of JSON input' or malformed payload. Hitting this on go-sdk v0.12.3.

kevin_eng: seen this before. bufio.Scanner defaults to 64KB max token. If a server chunk contains >64KB without a '\n' boundary, Scanner returns ErrTooLong and you end up with truncated data. Also Scanner expects delimiting token; chunked responses sometimes split JSON mid-object across TCP chunks.

maria_runtime: additional wrinkle: our SDK had a compatibility helper that used Scanner with ScanBytes('\n') split to treat SSE-like lines. But when model outputs are compact (no newlines) things get merged. That helper also tried to be stateful and recombine partial tokens — which is fragile with retries.

sam_support: logs from the customer: 
```
error: json: unexpected end of JSON input
pkg: github.com/redwood/go-sdk/stream.Reader
scan error: bufio.Scanner: token too long
http: response body read error: EOF
```

lina_customer: we also see duplicated partial events when we enable our own retry wrapper — it retries after a read error and the server re-sends from start, so we concat fragments and end up with combined JSON like `}{` in the middle.

kevin_eng: two separate problems: 1) Scanner token size / split semantics, 2) retry semantics causing overlapping fragments. Short-term workaround: use json.Decoder on the underlying io.Reader instead of Scanner. Decoder handles streaming JSON tokens and doesn't have the 64KB hard cap. Example: 
```
dec := json.NewDecoder(body)
for {
    var evt map[string]interface{}
    if err := dec.Decode(&evt); err == io.EOF { break }
    if err != nil { log.Fatal(err) }
    handle(evt)
}
```

maria_runtime: longer-term fix: we should stop using bufio.Scanner in the SDK streaming path. Also add a safe retry policy: only retry if no bytes were consumed on the client side (i.e., failure before first read) OR the server supports resume tokens. For now, disable automatic retry on streaming endpoints in go-sdk until we replace the implementation.

sam_support: can we provide a patch the customer can drop in? They want a quick workaround besides switching to Decoder.

kevin_eng: yes — two options to give them: 1) increase Scanner buffer & custom split function to merge across chunks: 
```
scanner := bufio.NewScanner(body)
max := 2 * 1024 * 1024 // 2MB
buf := make([]byte, 0, 64*1024)
scanner.Buffer(buf, max)
// custom split to return whole JSON objects or fall back
```
But that is brittle. 2) Better: replace scan loop with io.Reader + json.Decoder as above. Provide sample wrapper in support note.

lina_customer: switching to json.Decoder fixed our replay repro locally. Also FYI the HTTP response had `Transfer-Encoding: chunked` and Content-Length absent — so chunk boundaries are definitely arbitrary.

maria_runtime: action items: 
- kevin to draft a go-sdk patch that swaps Scanner->Decoder in streaming client and add unit tests for large single-object streams (deadline EOD).
- I will add a feature flag to disable streaming retries in 0.12.x patch and document the workaround.
- sam to send the temporary snippet to Lina.

kevin_eng: putting small repro test into PR: reads a 1.5MB JSON object streamed in random chunk sizes and asserts Decoder decodes successfully. Also add a note about not retrying mid-stream.

bot-deploy: deploy request queued for canary env (ref: deploy/streaming-fix-180520).

sam_support: Lina — please try the patch/decoder snippet I DM'd. If that clears it we'll mark as resolved and track SDK patch release. Thanks for the detailed repro logs, they made this quick to root cause. :tada:
